nodes.label: S0 — scaffold, TestFlight (stage doc, referenced)
nodes.rationale: Empty app installs and renders one shared-package string first, so a Metro/workspace-resolution failure is caught in ten minutes instead of a bewildering afternoon at S4.

nodes.label: D6 — Scaffold template: default
nodes.rationale: The default template wires expo-router, typed routes and @expo/ui in one pass, matching D3; retrofitting later means changing the entry point mid-stage.

nodes.label: D7 — One EAS project, three bundle-id variants
nodes.rationale: Sharing one EAS slug/project across dev/preview/production avoids fragmenting into three projects and breaking `eas build --profile`; unset APP_VARIANT must mean production so no command silently ships a dev bundle id.

nodes.label: D3 — Component strategy: Expo UI
nodes.rationale: Expo UI's SwiftUI/Compose APIs went stable in SDK 56 and ship in the default template, so it costs nothing alongside D6; iOS-only per D2 keeps the still-experimental universal/web implementation out of scope.

nodes.label: D8 — Expo SDK 57
nodes.rationale: RN 0.86/SDK 57 is a deliberately small release with no breaking changes from 0.85, and create-expo-app scaffolds it by default.

nodes.label: D9 — TestFlight deferred to S7; ship S0 on internal distribution
nodes.rationale: The unresolved residual is Apple account/paperwork, not code — a preview build already exercises the same Release binary, bundle, native modules and signing mechanics except store-distribution identity.
